result.competitor: XBOW (XBOW USA Inc.) — autonomous offensive-security / AI pentesting platform
result.summary: XBOW's buyer-facing pitch is a single machine: point it at a target + context and it runs a five-stage autonomous loop — Learn (CONTEXT_INGEST) → Map (live attack-surface map) → Coordinate (a central decision-engine that plans what/where/order and dispatches a fleet) → Attack (many short-lived, bias-reset agents exploiting and CHAINING in parallel with an offensive toolkit + steerable headless browser) → Prove (independent validator agents that confirm exploitability before any finding surfaces). The entire commercial thesis is PROOF, not detection: "Frontier models find vulnerabilities. A platform proves them." The differentiating machinery a buyer actually pays for is the validator/proof layer (independent re-check, execution-confirmed where possible), the per-finding "case file" (chained path + working exploit + full agent decision log + remediation, "nothing hidden behind a severity score"), production-safe/scoped/audited execution, and portfolio-scale surface discovery + dedup. Everything else (model routing, API/webhooks, compliance) is framed as enterprise wrapping around that proof core. Confidence HIGH that these are XBOW's marketed mechanisms; MEDIUM that they run exactly as described in the product (most detail is first-party marketing + one detailed named case study, with the raw benchmark score explicitly disclaimed by XBOW itself and third-party research showing the underlying task class is tractable for generic coding agents — i.e. the defensible moat is proof/validation/orchestration, not a superior model).

mechanisms.mechanism: Point-at-URL plus optional context (docs, credentials, API specs, architecture notes; 'the more you give it, the deeper it goes'). Builds a live map of applications/endpoints/parameters/auth flows. A central 'coordinator' decision engine decides what to test, where, and in what order and directs the fleet. 'Thousands of agents attack in parallel.' Independent validators confirm exploitability last. Positioned explicitly as 'exploitation, not pattern-matching.'

mechanisms.mechanism: Coordinator gives ongoing orchestration + a decision engine that 'debriefs agents and prioritizes.' Attack agents are short-lived, focused workers 'retired after each mission to avoid bias.' Validator agents are a distinct role that independently re-checks a claimed exploit. Three-role split (plan / attack / prove) rather than one monolithic model call.

mechanisms.mechanism: Links discrete findings into ONE working attack path ('connective tissue between bugs') rather than a flat list. Buyer-facing exemplar (Moderna, sanitized to capability level): source-read -> unrotated exposed API key -> authenticated API probing -> malformed-input handling cascading into the routing/gateway layer -> confirmed IDOR, full chain built in under 18 hours; human reviewers afterward confirmed a confidentiality impact in addition to the availability impact.

mechanisms.mechanism: Automated peer-reviewer 'validators' confirm each finding before it reaches the customer. Two flavors described: (1) purpose-built programmatic checks, (2) LLM-based peer review. Explicitly targets both scanner-style guesses and AI-hallucination false positives. Marketed as the actual durable product: 'Frontier models find vulnerabilities. A platform proves them' / 'proof, not a flood of maybes.'

For XSS, a real headless browser visits the target site and confirms the JavaScript payload actually executed, rather than trusting a reflection/pattern match. A 'steerable headless browser' is named as part of the offensive toolkit for reaching non-obvious paths. This is the buyer-facing standard for turning a candidate into proven risk.

Every finding ships as a complete, reproducible trace: the chained attack path, the working exploit, and a full log of every decision/tactic the agents took, plus developer-ready remediation. 'Nothing is hidden behind a severity score. You see the whole kill chain.' The platform page embeds a fully worked interactive trace (agent narration + reproduced scripts) as the richest proof-of-how-it-works artifact.

Scope/policy parsing (LLM + manual curation of non-machine-readable policies); a target-scoring system weighting WAF presence, HTTP status/redirect behavior, auth forms, reachable-endpoint count, tech stack, etc.; asset deduplication via SimHash (content similarity) + headless-browser screenshots + imagehash (visual similarity) to group cloned/staging environments and avoid wasted effort. Built during HackerOne dogfooding; now the substrate for the credential-less, black-box 'Autonomous Exposure Management' whole-estate product.
mechanisms.confidence: HIGH as described infra; MEDIUM that all of it is productized in the SaaS today

mechanisms.mechanism: Routes each task to 'the best model' and adopts new frontier models as they ship; pitched as no vendor lock-in and no migration project, with the platform (proof, safety, coverage, orchestration, cost control) framed as the durable value over any single underlying LLM.

Customer-defined scope XBOW operates strictly within; 'safe validation' using production-safe challenges designed to avoid modifying data or disrupting systems; every agent action logged and reviewable; human review before findings surface; board- and auditor-ready reporting; deployment aligned to data separation/residency + compliance (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIS 2; '40+ frameworks'). Directly answers the buyer objection to running autonomous exploitation in production.

result.role: WS-4 Chain-machinery AUDITOR (audit stage) — Abhedi Red, branch feat/alpha-observability @ f75608f
result.summary: Abhedi has TWO distinct, deterministic (no-LLM) chain subsystems, and they answer H3 differently. (1) The CHAIN GRAPH (chain/service.py + chain/capabilities.py) is PURE GRAPH INFERENCE over a static capability table: build_graph reads verified findings from findings.jsonl, maps vuln_class→Capability via GRANTS, mints one ChainNode per granted capability, and mints ChainEdge rows from the ENABLES adjacency. It is DEFAULT-ON (scanner_chain_synthesis=True, compose :-true) and feeds the report's "Candidate / reachability (not executed end-to-end)" section. (2) The CHAIN FLOOR (chain/floor.py) is the only part that ACTUALLY FIRES a next-hop probe from a confirmed primitive; it is DEFAULT-OFF via env SCANNER_ENGINE_CHAIN_FLOOR (compose :-0, NOT set in override.yml), so in a stock deploy it never runs. H3 VERDICT: the chain does NOT carry a proof ARTIFACT into hop N+1. The GRAPH edge is a pure table lookup (edge_rationale is a static template sentence); the proof (attrs.proof_of_concept) rides on each node as a decoration only, never as an input to next-hop inference. The FLOOR carries the source finding's LOCATION (url, param) — not its evidence object — into a FRESHLY, independently-fired hop N+1 request that re-proves from scratch. The executed_chain finding (_write_executed_chain) is a TEXTUAL composition: a PoC string naming source→cap→follow-on, with NO parent finding_id linkage, NO proof_capsule, NO evidence_paths, and NO replay contract. There is NO proof-type enum anywhere (Capability=capability tokens, VulnClass=vuln classes, proof state is signaled by string fields like verification_method='executed_chain'). Design implication: proof-artifact carry, parent-finding linkage, and a re-runnable chain capsule are the DELTA the designer must add — they do not exist today (harvest the graph + floor + capability table; do not rebuild them).
current_state: TWO subsystems, not one. GRAPH: chain/service.py build_graph:123-234 (nodes+edges) / synthesize_chains:325-346 / enumerate_ranked_chains:264-322. FLOOR: chain/floor.py run_chain_floor:407-454. capabilities.py:22-216 is the shared static table (Capability StrEnum, GRANTS, ENABLES, EDGE_RATIONALE). [CODE]

GRAPH synthesis is graph-only. build_graph derives node capabilities DETERMINISTICALLY from vuln_class via capabilities_for/GRANTS (service.py:150) and derives edges purely from reachable_from/ENABLES (service.py:216-228). The docstring is explicit: 'there is no model free-text gained/prerequisite string-matching anymore' (service.py:139-141). Edges carry only edge_rationale(src_cap,vc) — a STATIC template sentence from EDGE_RATIONALE (capabilities.py:106-167), NOT derived from the source's actual evidence. [CODE]

The proof rides on a node but is NOT an input to the next hop. build_graph binds proof to each ChainNode.attrs: proof_of_concept (capped 4000, service.py:167-173), evidence_path, and optional reasoning (attacker_narrative, service.py:177-179). This is a per-node DECORATION for the report; the ENABLES edge inference never reads it. [CODE]

FLOOR carries LOCATION, not artifact. run_chain_floor reads confirmed findings (_read_confirmed:146-162, same verified+proof_of_concept gate as build_graph), extracts (url,param) via _finding_target:190-201, and for each capability fires a FRESH deterministic curl that re-proves independently (e.g. _hop_metadata injects _METADATA_URLS into the param and regex-matches the NEW response body, floor.py:232-280). Hop N's evidence object never enters hop N+1's request or evidence. [CODE]

FLOOR hops are a static capability→probe table: _HOPS (floor.py:397-404) maps METADATA_ACCESS→(_hop_metadata,_hop_bucket), CLOUD_STORAGE→_hop_bucket, FILE_READ→_hop_file_read, REDIRECT→_hop_redirect, INTERNAL_HTTP→_hop_internal, CREDENTIAL→_hop_credential. Each hop self-proves→_write_finding, else emits _signal. Bounded by seen_hops (Father-owned, per (cap,url,param), floor.py:437-440) + _MAX_HOPS=40 (floor.py:102) + per-wave depth cap. [CODE]

executed_chain finding is a TEXTUAL composition, not an evidence-linked capsule. _write_executed_chain (floor.py:204-228) writes proof_of_concept as a prose string ('CONFIRMED {src_class} at {url} → {cap.value} → PROVED {follow}...'), inherits the follow-on hop's CWE, and sets verification_method='executed_chain', detected_by_tool='chain'. It writes NO evidence_paths, NO proof_capsule, and NO parent finding_id — the source is referenced only by name in the string. [CODE]

NO proof-type enum exists. The only chain enum is Capability (StrEnum, capabilities.py:22-33) = capability tokens. Proof state is signaled by free string fields: verification_method='executed_chain' (floor.py:225), tool='chain:ssrf-metadata'/'chain:lfi-secrets' (floor.py:258,335), category='executed_chain'. [CODE]

Parent-finding linkage is partial and lossy. GRAPH: ChainNode.finding_id is a nullable UUID column with NO DB ForeignKey (tenant.py:306); it is set only when the JSONL finding already carries a uuid finding_id (service.py:183 _is_uuid(fid) else None). ChainEdge.from_node/to_node ARE real FKs (tenant.py:331-332) — so node→node linkage exists, but node→finding often does not. FLOOR: the executed_chain row has zero finding-id linkage. [CODE]

Report narrative today (reporting/service.py). '## Attack chains (what an attacker can chain)' has two subsections: '### Executed (proven end-to-end)' from executed_chains (verified executed_chain findings, service.py:298-306,528-542) and '### Candidate / reachability (not executed end-to-end)' from chain_narratives (the graph walk, service.py:297,543-554). Each candidate line is 'Chain: cap1 → cap2 → cap3' then per-step 'prev → cap: <rationale><step_detail>' where rationale is the static EDGE_RATIONALE sentence and step_detail adds title/endpoint/poc/evidence. Fallback (single edges only) narrates raw adjacency 'from → to: rationale' (service.py:555-559). [CODE]

DEFAULT-ON: scanner_chain_synthesis=True (config.py:149), compose SCANNER_CHAIN_SYNTHESIS :-true (docker-compose.yml:227) — the GRAPH build + candidate-chain report is LIVE in stock prod (finalize.py:333-352, father.py live-tick :1061-1068). [CODE][QUERY]

DEFAULT-OFF: the FLOOR is env-gated SCANNER_ENGINE_CHAIN_FLOOR default '0' (father.py:487-491), compose :-0 (docker-compose.yml:140), NOT set in override.yml. father._run_chain_floor:1620 is the ONLY caller of run_chain_floor and self-gates on it, so the floor NEVER fires in prod OR the dev override. [CODE][QUERY]

Escalation re-loop consumes the GRAPH, not proof artifacts. engine/escalation.py:37-50 calls build_graph then newly_high_impact (service.py:237-246, HIGH_IMPACT set capabilities.py:96-98) to detect newly-arrived high-impact capabilities and reopen ledger classes via cells_unlocked_by (service.py:249-254). questions.q: H3(a): Is a chain synthesized as pure graph over a capability table, or does a confirmed primitive carry a PROOF ARTIFACT (the actual evidence object) into hop N+1's prompt/evidence?
questions.answer: Pure graph + location. The GRAPH (chain/service.py) is a pure walk over the GRANTS/ENABLES capability table; the FLOOR (chain/floor.py) carries the source finding's (url,param) LOCATION and fires a fresh independently-re-proving request. Neither carries hop N's evidence OBJECT into hop N+1. The proof only rides on a node as a display decoration (service.py:167-179).

hypotheses.note: Browser client-side capability stops at instrument-based DOM-XSS + prototype-pollution + storage-leak (3 classes, single-page each). No browser-driven multi-step SPA state-change (login->navigate->act->assert) oracle. The only multi-step browser flows are login primitives (_try_login form/identifier-first; _try_sso_login federated, gated) whose job is to authenticate the crawl, not to perform-then-assert an app state transition. NUANCE: a multi-step STATE-CARRYING flow oracle DOES exist for the HTTP layer (channels.py replay_sequences: capture order_id step2 -> feed step4, verdicts step_auth_bypassed/workflow_skip_succeeded/replay_succeeded) but it runs via curl/_fire over /exec, is NOT browser/SPA-driven, and ships default-OFF (scanner_channel_oracles_enabled). So the missing capability is specifically 'assert a client-side/SPA state change after an authed in-browser action', e.g. a JS-only privilege toggle or client-routed workflow bypass whose effect never surfaces in a raw HTTP request/response pair.

None of the three named classes is skill-only. GraphQL authz = full pure-code oracle (graphql_authz.py: field_authz_verdict/bopla_exposure/bopla_writability/depth_unlimited/batch_unlimited). WebSocket(+SSE+webhook) = pure-code oracle (channels.py: channel_auth_open/cross_user_leak/webhook_sig_bypassed/webhook_replayable). JWT/OAuth/session = pure-code oracle (exploit_floor.py: parse_jwt_forge/parse_pkce_missing/parse_session_fixation/parse_session_no_rotation/parse_revoked_replay). Even AI/MCP has deterministic oracles (ai_redteam canary_in_output/tool_invoked). The correct restatement: these are 'code-oracle-exists-but-default-OFF', not 'skill-only'. The gap a buyer would notice is coverage-shipped, not coverage-absent: a stock deploy runs the always-on floor + default-ON browser instrument/HAR-slice, but NOT GraphQL/WS/JWT-OAuth-session/two-identity/AI oracles unless an operator flips the flag.

result.summary: CONFIRMED the WS-1 "coverage thrash" mechanism empirically — but reframed by the data into TWO coupled pathologies, not one. (1) RECLAIM THRASH: cells cycle untested->testing(claim,attempts++)->lease-expire->reclaim->testing without terminalizing. The DB `ledger_cell.attempts` counter (each claim_cells does attempts+=1) proves it: applicable cells claimed >=2x = 622/2719 (23%) on prior scan 68a58881, 727/2122 (34%) on infinity 1f5fe7c8, and 428/2916 (15%, still climbing at only max=3 attempts 7h in) on the LIVE scan 84aea81a. LIVE smoking gun: 1654/1703 (97%) of currently-`testing` cells sit in expired-lease limbo (claimed_by set, lease_expires_at < now()) = exactly the re-claimable state, yet their last_progress is <5min because a periodic resolve pass (LIVE_CONVERGENCE, SYNC_INTERVAL_S=120) bumps last_progress independent of the lease — so the last_progress-based stuck-detector (STUCK_WINDOW_S=1200) never fires while the lease-based claim gate keeps re-handing them. hypotheses.id: WS1-coverage-thrash: cells cycle claim/reclaim without terminalizing, stalling coverage
hypotheses.note: Reclaim thrash is real and measured (23-34% of applicable cells claimed >=2x; 97% of live testing cells in re-claimable limbo). BUT the dominant coverage-stall driver in FINALIZED scans is the coupled STARVATION: 39%/22% of applicable cells are never claimed once and are swept to 'attempted' unreached at finalize. Capacity concentrates on re-working a subset while another subset is never reached. The attempt-cap (6) is rarely hit, so cap-absorption is a minor contributor.

hypotheses.id: attempt-cap absorbs thrashed cells to 'attempted' during the run
hypotheses.note: Cap absorption requires attempts>=cap(6); only ~1-2 cells reached 6 on 68a58881 and ~152 on 1f5fe7c8. 81%/55% of 'attempted' cells have attempts=0 -> they came from finalize retire-unreached (finalize.py:454-460), not the reclaim cap. The cap is not doing the in-run termination its docstring claims for these runs.

Stuck-detection is last_progress-based (STUCK_WINDOW_S=1200) but a periodic resolve pass bumps last_progress independent of the lease, so all 1654 limbo cells read <5min 'fresh' and are never flagged, while the lease-based claim gate re-hands them.

defects.title: last_progress and lease_expires_at are two disagreeing clocks -> stuck-detection blind to lease-limbo reclaim thrash
defects.mechanism: claim_cells stamps both last_progress and lease_expires_at; resolve_cells (fired every SYNC_INTERVAL_S=120 by LIVE_CONVERGENCE) bumps last_progress on every matched cell but never the lease. A cell claimed >30min ago (lease expired -> re-claimable) still reads last_progress<5min, so the last_progress-based stuck-detector (STUCK_WINDOW_S=1200) never preempts it while the lease-based claim gate keeps re-handing it. Live: 1654/1703 testing cells in exactly this state.
defects.module_flag: ledger/service.py claim_cells:1393-1417 vs resolve_cells:1028; father stuck-detection STUCK_WINDOW_S. Fix would be flag-gated default-OFF (e.g. tie stuck-detection to lease_expires_at, or a scanner_ledger_progress_extends_lease knob).
defects.blast_radius: Coverage stalls: capacity re-claims warm-but-stale cells instead of untested ones; masks genuine hangs.

defects.title: 'attempted' terminal state conflates reclaim-exhaustion with never-reached starvation -> honest-coverage and thrash metrics are muddled
defects.mechanism: Two code paths write state='attempted': (a) release/reclaim when attempts>=cap (real exhaustion), (b) finalize.py:454-460 retire-unreached (scanner_finalize_retire_unreached=True) sweeping any applicable untested/empty-testing cell at scan end. In finalized scans (b) dominates (81%/55% of 'attempted' have attempts=0). A reader counting 'attempted' as 'thrashed to death' overstates thrash and hides that 22-39% of the surface was never tested.
defects.module_flag: finalize.py:454-460 (scanner_finalize_retire_unreached, default True) + ledger release/reclaim cap absorption. Distinguish with a separate na_reason/state (e.g. 'unreached' vs 'attempted') behind a default-OFF flag; report.py coverage already treats attempted as not-resolved.
defects.blast_radius: Buyer-visible coverage %: a scan that reached completed can have 22-39% of applicable cells never probed, reported only as 'attempted'.

defects.title: Capacity concentration: fleet re-claims a ~600-720 cell subset up to 6x while a comparable subset is never claimed once
defects.mechanism: claim_cells orders by vuln_class priority then updated_at then cell_id and re-hands expired-lease cells (which keep getting updated_at/last_progress bumped) ahead of never-touched cells that share priority. Net: the same subset is reclaimed repeatedly (attempts 2-6) while low-priority-class cells starve to finalize retire-unreached.
defects.module_flag: ledger/service.py claim_cells ORDER BY :1403 (array_position(ranked) NULLS LAST, updated_at, cell_id). A default-OFF 'prefer attempts=0 within a priority tier' tiebreak (ORDER BY ... , attempts ASC, updated_at) would spread capacity to unreached cells without changing class priority.
defects.blast_radius: 22-39% unreached surface per scan; reclaim effort has diminishing returns (35-48% of reclaimed cells still never converge).
